name: Scarcity.AI
summary: Three Shopify urgency apps — low stock counter, countdown timer and live visitors counter — that read real data but let you choose which true number the shopper sees.
best_for: Shopify merchants who genuinely run low stock or timed promotions and want to surface that on the product page — the low stock counter is tied to real inventory, which makes it the honest one of the three when your stock actually is low
skip_if: your stock is not low and your sale does not end, because a claim a shopper would read as false is one the FTC treats as deceptive; or your brand sells on trust, where a blinking counter costs more in credibility than it returns
honest_knock:
All three read real data, which is worth saying before anything else — the low stock counter shows inventory levels and the visitors counter reads unique visitors, live traffic and product views. Nothing here invents a number.

But the visitors counter carries two settings that shape which true number a shopper sees. It can show the counter only after a set number of views, so a quiet product simply displays nothing rather than a small figure. And the time frame is yours to set, so 'twelve people viewed this' can mean twelve in five minutes or twelve since yesterday, presented identically. Neither setting fabricates anything; together they let you present a true number that a reasonable shopper would read as something else.

That distinction is where the legal line sits. The FTC treats false urgency and scarcity as deceptive practice under section 5 of the FTC Act, and the examples in its dark-patterns guidance are close to these mechanics: a low-stock claim when stock is plentiful, or a cart-activity figure well above the real one. The test is whether a reasonable consumer would be misled about a material fact. That test does not apply to the app; it applies to how you configure it, which means the compliance question lands on your desk rather than the developer's.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Monthly Plan… · per month for the low stock counter, or $41.91 a year
pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com, across all three listings) These are three separate apps from one developer, each installed and billed on its own. The Low Stock Counter is $4.99 a month or $41.91 a year at a stated 30% saving, with a 7-day trial; its free tier is Development Stores, meaning development and partner stores only rather than a working free plan. The Visitors Counter is $1.99 a month or $16.71 a year, with a genuine free plan that carries the counter itself, customisation, product-level targeting and holiday presets — the $1.99 adds an upsell banner for your most-viewed product, on a 3-day trial. The Countdown Timer listing shows a free tier and no paid ladder. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, who also publish Blocky, TiXel and Way. Ratings at the time of writing: 4.7 from 84 reviews on the low stock counter, 4.8 from 36 on the visitors counter and 5.0 from 22 on the countdown timer.
